reviews.text: Troll plays its premise too seriously to be any fun and it lacks any socio-critical muster to be an effective disaster film.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: “Troll” is as much fun as any of the recent films in Legendary Pictures’ MonsterVerse.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: With a perfect run time, some superb visuals, and a throughline of some brilliant mythology, Troll deserves to be watched.
reviews.author: Aaron Phillips

reviews.text: That often dismissed and maligned word “fun” defines “Troll” in a nutshell. It’s an eye-popping genre flick that delivers exactly what you expect from it. Nothing more; nothing less.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A goofier riff on 2014’s Godzilla, greatly in debt to the Roland Emmerich disaster textbook.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: “Troll” succeeds by getting back to basics. Like way, way back — all the way to the Old Norse.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: The film throws in some themes about sins committed in the name of Christianizing Norway and nature "pushing back" on human encroachments. But don't go looking for serious commentary in this movie (not that you would in a film called Troll).
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Uthaug seems to have learned the proper lessons from King Kong and Godzilla, as it builds tension well, supplies strong enough effects, and never leans too hard into camp or sincerity.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Troll does exactly what you are hoping for.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Rich in spectacle and mythology even if offering nothing we haven't seen before.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Troll is a fun jaunt through the Norweigan countryside filled with a path of destruction that’s very much like a Kaiju film. As a casual watch, this is decent and entertaining, but it’s not memorable or lasting.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: A great piece of unassuming monster mayhem, a refreshingly Nordic take on tropes and cliches that Hollywood has mined to the point of exhaustion over the years.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Troll is a low-key high-craft meat-&-potatoes addition to the kaiju canon.
reviews.author: Christian Valentin

reviews.text: Watching Troll is like engulfing a cherished comfort food meal. The film’s lack of nutritional value is frankly irrelevant compared to the charming spectacle Uthaug and company cultivate.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Troll is an effective and family-friendly monster movie, with bloodless combat and few scares.
reviews.author: James Field

reviews.text: The director handles well the different tempos of the film, creating intrigue even though we all know the Troll will be up to no good in no time... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: While the effects work is first-rate and the action efficiently handled, there is a frustrating lack of Scandinavian specificity on display.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text:
Entertaining and scary too,
this Norwegian film should please you.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Every single scene in Troll is cribbed wholesale from other movies, and very few of those other movies are any good.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Directed by the fabulously named Roar Uthaug, the new Norwegian language Netflix film Troll is a wonderful pastiche of American blockbusters.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Troll isn’t a big monster movie that takes itself too seriously. While conventional, there is enough fun and interesting lore to provide audiences with a good time.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Even though Troll doesn't squeeze all its possibilities to the max, it still gifts us great action scenes with the creature... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Feels faintly familiar, while refreshingly different, featuring new wrinkles that are well-considered and profoundly satisfying.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: While light on narrative, it’s when director Roar Uthaug embraces the film's monster that Troll reveals its magic.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: [I]f you can look past the cliché-ridden moments, Troll [is] a reasonably entertaining import for a Norwegian creature feature.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: It looks far better than this year’s Marvel offerings and follows Moonfall as one of this year’s silliest, but best disaster films.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: A decent ride of large-scale action and near-misses, sold with competent performances and cinematic energy.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Clearly, Uthaug is not taking all this entirely seriously, but he never pitches TROLL as a spoof. He takes spectacle seriously...and to that end, the visual effects of the troll and its devastation are first-rate.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Since a creature feature lives and dies by its monster, Troll has the clear advantage of conjuring a magnificent beast from Scandinavian folklore. Uthaug ultimately succeeds in developing a movie that’ll most likely please fans of giant creatures.
reviews.author: Marco Vito Oddo

synopsis: Deep inside the mountain of Dovre, something gigantic awakens after being trapped for a thousand years. Destroying everything in its path, the creature is fast approaching the capital of Norway. But how do you stop something you thought only existed in Norwegian folklore?
